detail.body:
### What does this PR do? Adds end-to-end **MXFP8 reinforcement learning on Blackwell (SM100)** to verl, for #5972: Megatron/Transformer Engine (TE) training with `fp8_recipe: mxfp8`, and MXFP8 rollout on **vLLM** and **SGLang**, for dense and MoE models. The design goal is train–inference consistency by construction. At every weight sync the rollout weights are quantized with **TE's own `MXFP8Quantizer`**, the function the learner applies to the weight operand of its forward GEMMs. The sampler therefore serves the learner's FP8 weight grid (E4M3 elements, E8M0 scale per 32-element block), not an independent re-quantization ("shared-grid" sync). | Part | What this PR adds | |---|---| | Training | `fp8_recipe: mxfp8` through the existing `override_transformer_config`. The one functional gap was THD sequence padding: TE's MXFP8 quantizer needs both GEMM dimensions divisible by 32, and the wgrad scale blocks run along the token dimension, so the per-sequence alignment becomes `lcm(32, align)` under MXFP8 (blockwise keeps `lcm(16, align)`). | | Shared quantizer | `verl/utils/mxfp8_quant.py`: TE `MXFP8Quantizer` (E4M3, row-wise 1×32 blocks, compact UE8M0 scales), used by both engines. `lm_head` and the token embedding stay BF16. | | vLLM rollout | Launches from the BF16 checkpoint with a config vLLM maps to its ModelOpt MXFP8 method; quantizes inside the vLLM worker at each sync; re-derives kernel layouts through verl's existing record/stage/reprocess cycle (dense and MoE methods registered); matches layer exclusions on module-path boundaries instead of vLLM 0.24's substring fallback. | | SGLang rollout | Launch override; quantizes on the trainer side before streaming; a refit loader re-runs post-processing for every MXFP8 layer whose backend keeps derived scale copies. | | Guards | A self-check after every sync (one dense layer and one MoE expert against a dequantized BF16 reference), a quantized-layer audit (learner vs. live engine, per parameter), and a step sentinel (NaN / KL > 1 / all responses truncated). All are no-ops unless rollout quantization is enabled. | Nothing changes unless MXFP8 is configured. Related: #5972, #4223, #5440, #7186. Fixes found while validating this PR and merged separately: #7986, #7987, #8062. ### Results at a glance Measured on NVIDIA B200 with Qwen3-8B (dense) and Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE), in four settings plus 17 controlled runs. Each configuration ran once (one seed), for 3–60 steps, so nothing here ranks final model quality. 1. **Matching buys consistency.** For an MXFP8 learner, an MXFP8 sampler on the learner's grid is *more* consistent than a BF16 sampler. - In one engine at fixed weights, train–rollout KL is **10.6% lower** with the sampler's qkv/o/down projections on the grid and **16.1% lower** [95% CI 14.1, 18.1] with every linear on the grid. - The synced weights equal the learner's FP8 forward weights **byte for byte**. - On MoE, verl's existing FP8-blockwise pipeline, whose sampler rounds onto a different grid, has **2×** the MXFP8 pipeline's KL from step 1. - BF16 end to end remains 2.5–10× more consistent. 2. **Speed is conditional.** - MXFP8 cuts the learner's per-token cost (`update_actor` −43%), but adds a fixed **cost per micro-batch** (~51 ms per forward–backward micro-batch), so it pays off only above **~4.5k tokens per micro-batch**. - A sweep on identical replayed data confirms the per-micro-batch form. A trace shows the GPU idle, **waiting for the host to issue work**, for most of the added time. - End to end: MoE step **−10.7%** (generation −24%), dense long-sequence step −6.4%, dense short-sequence step **+5.1%**. 3. **Correctness must be checked against the live engine.** - Seven failures surfaced on B200; five were silent (exit 0, normal-looking metrics). - Each of the four silent failures that reached a run is caught by at least one guard. The two that occurred after the guards were in place were caught at their first opportunity, each by a different guard, and a divergence alarm alone would have missed both. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+mxfp8 - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+5972+in%3Abody - **Not a duplicate.** - **#7186** (draft) adds MXFP8 SGLang rollout with an independent Triton quantizer. This PR differs in three ways: - it quantizes rollout weights with TE's quantizer, so the sampler holds the learner's grid; this is measured byte for byte below; - it ships the training side and both rollout engines as one mode; - it reuses verl's existing FP8 rollout machinery instead of parallel paths. - **#7918** is this PR's exact exclusion matcher on its own, not wired in, so that it can be reviewed separately. This PR includes the matcher and enables it for verl-generated MXFP8 configs. - **#7971** (draft) is NVFP4, a different format. - The Ascend MXFP8 PRs (#4679, #5608) touch only NPU paths. - [x] PR title formatted as `[megatron, rollout] feat: MXFP8 training and SGLang/vLLM rollout` ### Test CPU unit tests: the first ten files are added in this PR, and the last is the existing test of the preprocess path it changes. TE, vLLM and SGLang are stubbed where needed. ```bash python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_quant_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_quant_sentinel_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_quant_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py -q # 136 passed, 1 skipped (GPU-only case), on f28adc0c ``` `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, license, docstring, config generation). The B200 end-to-end runs are below. ### B200 validation #### Setup | | A | B | C | D | Controlled runs | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Model | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8) | Qwen3-8B | | Data | gsm8k | DAPO-Math-17k | gsm8k | DAPO-Math-17k | gsm8k | | GPUs | 2×B200, TP2 | 2×B200, TP2 | 2×B200, TP2 | 4×B200, TP2 × EP2 | 2×B200, TP2 | | Rollout | vLLM 0.24 | vLLM 0.24, fp8 KV cache (all arms) | SGLang 0.5.12 | vLLM 0.24 | vLLM 0.24 | | Response cap | 2048 | 8192 | 2048 | 8192 | 2048 | | Steps | 60 | 32 | 30 | 10 | 3–12 | "X/Y" below means learner precision X, sampler precision Y; FP8-TW is TE's per-tensor FP8 and FP8-BW verl's FP8 end-to-end blockwise recipe. - **Shared by all runs:** GRPO, 64 prompts × 8 samples per step, mini-batch 32 prompts, lr 1e-6, KL loss 0.001 (`low_var_kl`), and the same seed and data order within a setting. - **Arms per setting:** - A–C: BF16/BF16, FP8-TW/BF16 and MXFP8/MXFP8. - A also has MXFP8/BF16, the MXFP8 learner with an unquantized sampler. - D adds FP8-BW/FP8-BW. - **Partial matching in A and B.** The vLLM sampler there kept `gate_up_proj` in BF16, through the exclusion bug F2 that this PR fixes. The SGLang (C) and MoE (D) samplers put every decoder linear on the grid, and the controlled matching experiment adds a fully matched vLLM sampler. - **The controlled runs** use A's configuration, with two designs: - a **matching experiment**: four samplers at learning rate 0, so the weights stay at the checkpoint; - a **micro-batch sweep**: replayed identical data, update micro-batches of 1, 2, 4 and 8 sequences plus a half batch, for a BF16 and an MXFP8 learner, with two Nsight Systems profiling runs. - **Statistics.** - Intervals come from bootstrapping prompts within one run per arm. - "±" values are within-run standard errors. - None of these replaces independent seeds. #### 1. Consistency: what matching buys **Controlled matching experiment.** The setup: - one engine (vLLM) and one MXFP8 learner recipe, at learning rate 0, with the same 64 prompts per step in every arm; - the samplers differ only in how many decoder linears are on the learner's grid; - KL is pooled over steps 2–10 (576 prompts × 8 samples), with 95% intervals from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of prompts, paired across arms. | Sampler | KL, step 1 | KL | KL reduction vs. BF16 sampler | k3 reduction | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16/BF16 (reference) | 0.00067 | 0.00072 | | | | MXFP8 learner, BF16 sampler | 0.00854 | 0.00812 | | | | MXFP8/MXFP8, `gate_up_proj` in BF16 | 0.00719 | 0.00726 | 10.6% [8.6, 12.7] | 10.2% [8.7, 11.7] | | MXFP8/MXFP8, every linear on the grid | 0.00697 | 0.00682 | **16.1% [14.1, 18.1]** | 15.5% [14.1, 16.9] | - **What the reduction measures.** The fully matched sampler is 6.1% [3.9, 8.3] below the partially matched one. Log-perplexity and Pearson correlation agree; token-level χ² agrees in direction, but its intervals include zero for each single step of matching. Putting a layer on the grid changes its weights, the quantization of its input activations and its GEMM kernel at once, so the 16% belongs to the recipe as a whole, not to the weight grid alone. - **Byte check.** Bytes were compared at two syncs: - the fully matched run's 11th sync, at learning rate 0; - a sweep run's 7th sync, after 14 optimizer updates at 1e-6. Each covers layers 0, 17 and 35, all four projections, both TP ranks. The engine's E4M3 weights and E8M0 scales equal TE's quantization of the synced weights. The post-processed kernel layouts hold the same bytes, and the learner's cached FP8 forward weights equal the same quantization: **0 of ~600 MB differ** in every comparison. - **The check would catch a stale sampler.** The updates before the second sync had changed 0.84% of the FP8 bytes (at least 0.6% of every matrix), so a sampler still holding the step-0 weights would have failed every comparison. - **The two quantizers agree.** TE's quantizer and vLLM's own MXFP8 quantizer agree byte for byte on all 252 linear weights of Qwen3-8B (6.95 B elements) and on boundary cases. - **What remains.** With the weights byte-identical, 84% of the BF16-sampler mismatch remains. It most likely comes from activation quantization acting on slightly different inputs and from the two engines' different kernels, not from stored weights. **Across settings.** KL at step 1, where all arms of a setting hold the same weights, and over the last 10 steps: | Setting | BF16/BF16 | FP8-TW/BF16 | MXFP8/BF16 | FP8-BW/FP8-BW | MXFP8/MXFP8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A (vLLM) | 0.00066 → 0.00069 | 0.00859 → 0.01217 | 0.00828 → 0.00864 | | 0.00723 → 0.00693 (gate_up BF16) | | C (SGLang) | 0.00064 (step 1) | 0.00881 (step 1) | | | 0.00681 → 0.00670 (all matched) | | B (vLLM, fp8 KV) | 0.00610 → 0.00882 | 0.00915 → 0.02969 | | | 0.00927 → 0.00878 (gate_up BF16) | | D (MoE, vLLM) | 0.00174 → 0.00177 | 0.00519 → 0.00584 | | 0.00921 → 0.00899 | 0.00446 → 0.00449 (all matched) | - **Shared-grid vs. per-tensor FP8.** Among low-precision pipelines, the shared-grid pipeline is the most consistent in every setting. Its last-10-step KL is 43% (A), 70% (B), 46% (C) and 23% (D) below FP8-TW/BF16. At step 1 the margin is smaller, 16% (A), 23% (C), 14% (D) and none in B, because most of the late margin is the per-tensor recipe's drift: its KL grows 3.1× over B's 32 steps, while MXFP8's stays flat. - **Different grids double the mismatch.** On Blackwell, FP8-BW's learner must use power-of-two block scales while its sampler quantizes with FP32 scales, so the two sides round the same weight differently. Its KL is 2× MXFP8's at step 1, before the runs diverge. - **BF16 floor.** BF16 end to end stays ~10× (A) and 2.5× (D) more consistent. B's fp8 KV cache raises its BF16 floor. #### 2. Speed: when MXFP8 pays off **A cost per micro-batch.** In RL the tokens per step `T` change as responses shorten (they halve over setting A), so per-step and per-token times mislead. Instead, each stage's time is fitted as `t = F + c·T` over the run's steps. For setting A's `update_actor` (steps 4–60, ± standard errors): | Arm | F (s) | c (µs/token) | added cost per micro-batch, Δδ (ms) | break-even m* = Δδ/Δc (tokens per micro-batch) | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 | 12.31 ± 0.30 | 26.74 ± 0.69 | | | | FP8-TW | 18.10 ± 0.28 | 14.60 ± 0.66 | 45.3 | 3,726 ± 61 | | MXFP8 | 18.89 ± 0.24 | 15.38 ± 0.56 | 51.5 | **4,527 ± 108** | A single run cannot tell a per-step cost from a per-micro-batch one. Three observations favor per-micro-batch: - the added fixed costs of the old-log-prob and update stages are consistent with a per-micro-batch cost, given their micro-batch counts (a consistency check, not a proof); - on a slower-CPU host the same recipe is a net loss; - the per-micro-batch form predicts held-out setting B, at ~12.2k tokens per micro-batch, better than a per-step form. For MXFP8 it predicts per-token savings of 9.0% (old log-prob) and 15.9% (update), against 9.1% and 11.9% measured; a per-step model predicts 13.2% and 20.9%. The recipe therefore pays off above **m\* ≈ 4.5k tokens per micro-batch** on this model and host. **Controlled sweep.** The same replayed token data runs at every step, and only the micro-batch size changes (update-stage time per step, mean of steps 2–6, ± SE over 5 paired steps). The last two columns predict the difference from setting A's constants: | Micro-batch (tokens) | micro-batches per step | BF16 (s) | MXFP8 (s) | MXFP8 − BF16 (s) | predicted, per-micro-batch cost | predicted, per-step cost | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 seq (1.3k) | 512 | 69.12 | 84.49 | +15.37 ± 0.44 | +18.9 | −0.9 | | 2 seq (2.6k) | 256 | 42.90 | 48.71 | +5.81 ± 0.97 | +5.7 | −0.9 | | 4 seq (5.2k) | 128 | 32.72 | 33.36 | +0.64 ± 0.91 | −0.9 | −0.9 | | 8 seq (10.3k) | 64 | 32.47 | 24.86 | −7.61 ± 1.68 | −4.2 | −0.9 | | 4 seq, half batch (5.2k) | 64 | 17.43 | 16.55 | −0.88 ± 0.75 | −0.5 | +2.8 | - **The difference grows with the number of micro-batches,** as a per-micro-batch cost predicts. Fitted on the sweep alone, the added cost is Δδ = 47.0 ± 4.5 ms per micro-batch (setting A: 51.5). - **There is no per-step part.** The sweep's per-step term is Δa = −0.10 ± 3.21 s. - **The crossing.** It sits near 5k tokens, but the sweep does not pin m\* down by itself (2.8k–7.6k under resampling). - **Caveat at 8 sequences.** BF16 does not speed up from 4 to 8 sequences, so part of MXFP8's lead there is BF16's slowdown. **Where the added time goes.** From Nsight Systems on the update stage, 1-sequence micro-batches, rank 0, per micro-batch: | | BF16 | MXFP8 | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | wall time under the profiler (ms) | 159.3 | 202.6 | **+43.4** | | GPU busy: kernels and copies, merged across streams | 69.6 | 75.5 | +5.9 | | no GPU operation running | 89.7 | 127.1 | +37.4 | | — host had not yet issued the next operation | 68.8 | 99.4 | **+30.6** | | — issued, not yet started (launch latency) | 16.4 | 22.7 | +6.3 | | — issued earlier, waiting on other work | 4.6 | 5.1 | +0.5 | | kernel launches | 4,139 | 5,051 | +912 | | wall time without the profiler (ms) | 135.0 | 165.0 | +30.0 | - **The extra kernels are cheap on the GPU.** MXFP8 launches 912 more kernels per micro-batch. 325 are activation and gradient quantizations, and 576 rearrange block scales into the GEMM's layout: 288 for the cached weights and 288 for tensors all-gathered under sequence parallelism. Their 4.8 ms and the longer NCCL kernels (+5.1 ms) are mostly offset by the FP8 GEMMs (−7.1 ms), so the GPU is busy only 5.9 ms longer. - **The cost is host work between GPU operations.** While the GPU waited, the issuing thread was outside every traced call (CUDA API, TE C++, NCCL), that is, in Python and framework code; synchronizing calls take the same time in both recipes. - **Remedies.** CUDA graphs or a faster host should lower m\*. TE ≥ 2.18 writes the cached weights' scales in the GEMM layout, which removes the 288 weight rearrangements, about 1.8 ms of profiled host time. **End to end.** Changes vs. BF16/BF16 on the same host: | | A: dense, gsm8k | B: dense, DAPO | D: MoE, DAPO | |---|---|---|---| | tokens per update micro-batch | ~3.4k (below m\*) | ~12.2k | dynamic batching, up to 20,480 per GPU | | step time | **+5.1%** | **−6.4%** | **−10.7%** | | `update_actor` | +6.9% | −12.1% | −9.4% | | old log-prob | −4.0% (~6.8k tokens per micro-batch) | −9.3% | −5.3% | | generation | −1.1% per token | −2.7% per token | **−23.8%** | | actor peak memory | +4.7% | +2.2% | +25% (60.0 → 75.0 GiB; FP8-BW: 74.6) | - **Setting A's update stage crosses m\* within one run.** In the first four steps, at 4.9–5.3k tokens per micro-batch, MXFP8 is 2.9% faster than BF16. Over the last ten, at 2.7k, it is 13.6% slower. - **Dense rollout speed.** This was measured only in the controlled runs, with every linear on the grid. The MXFP8 sampler generates 5.3% more tokens/s than the BF16 sampler of the same learner, but two identically configured BF16 samplers differ by 3.1%, so dense MXFP8 rollout shows no clear speed-up at this size. - **SGLang backend.** SGLang 0.5.12's default Triton MXFP8 GEMM makes generation 1.9× slower than BF16. Its FlashInfer CUTLASS backend, usable with weight sync after this PR's refit loader, cuts that to 1.4×. - **Weight-sync cost.** Quantizing at every sync adds ~1 s per step on the dense model (3.2 → 4.2 s in A) and 4 s on MoE including the self-check (3.5 → 7.5 s), 1–2% of a step. TE's quantization of all 252 dense weights takes ~11 ms of GPU time. Most of the added time is restoring parameters to a loadable layout (0.57 s) and re-deriving kernel layouts (0.49 s). - **Memory.** TE keeps FP8 copies next to the BF16 weights; on MoE the FP8-BW recipe costs the same. #### 3. Learning dynamics **Accuracy and reward.** There is no regression the data can resolve: - **A.** Held-out gsm8k accuracy after 60 steps is 0.9393 (MXFP8/MXFP8), 0.9363 (BF16), 0.9356 (MXFP8/BF16) and 0.9249 (FP8-TW). This is not an ordering: the MXFP8 sampler already scores 1.9 points higher on the untrained model, and repeating a configuration on another host moved accuracy by up to 2.0 points. - **B.** Reward, response length and truncation track BF16 (last-10 score 0.135 vs. 0.150). **Entropy** separates the recipes most clearly: - under MXFP8 the policy's entropy stays flat or rises (A −4%, B +4%, C +4%, D +6%); - under BF16 (A −49%) and FP8-TW (B −74%) it decays. The flatter policy is in the weights: the BF16 sampler of the MXFP8 learner sees it too. Step-matched checkpoints from different recipes are therefore not at the same point of training. #### 4. Correctness: what a weight sync must preserve After every sync the sampler must: - **C1** quantize exactly the learner's low-precision layers; - **C2** hold the learner's weight grid; - **C3** rebuild every kernel-specific derived layout; - **C4** update the storage CUDA graphs captured; - **C5** finish a streamed update completely; - **C6** produce finite probabilities and bounded divergence; - **C7** report every check's verdict. Each failure found on B200 broke one of these: | | Failure | Breaks | Symptom | Fix / caught now by | |---|---|---|---|---| | F1 | `lm_head` quantized in the sampler (silent) | C1 | NaN logits; reward 0.000 for 20 steps; every response at the length cap | keep `lm_head` and the embedding in BF16 (this PR); audit, sentinel | | F2 | router exclusion `mlp.gate` also excluded the dense `gate_up_proj` (silent) | C1 | none in the metrics; 56 of 311 parameters flagged on Qwen3-1.7B | exact module-path matching (this PR, also #7918); audit's engine re-check | | F3 | stale swizzled scales after sync, SGLang FlashInfer CUTLASS (silent) | C3 | held-out accuracy 0.000; KL 7.2 | refit loader re-runs post-processing (this PR); self-check, sentinel | | F4 | stale MoE expert layout after sync, vLLM TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE (silent) | C3 | expert probe error 1.74 (healthy 0.05); KL 0.047 | record same-shape repacks (#7986); self-check MoE probe | | F5 | BF16 MoE sync crashes on SM100 | C3 | crash at the first sync | in-place staging (#7987) | | F6 | FP32 block scales on SM100 | C2 | assertion at the first FP8 quantization | FP32 scales documented Hopper-only (#8062) | | F7 | guards ran but printed nothing (silent) | C7 | audit produced no output | dedicated log handler, forwarded level, warning when a check cannot run (this PR) | **The guards are complementary.** Of the four silent faults that reached a run: - only the audit's query of the live engine caught F2; its configured-rule half saw 28 of 28 layers agree; - only the self-check caught F4; - the sentinel fired on F1 (NaN) and F3 (KL 7.2) but stayed silent on F2 (KL 0.007–0.010) and F4 (KL 0.047), so divergence alarms cannot replace mechanism checks. **Healthy runs.** - The self-check read 0.026–0.027 (dense) and 0.049–0.052 (MoE expert), against its 0.25 tolerance; F4 read 1.739. - The audit agreed with the engine on all 69 and 18,867 parameters it checked. - The only false alarm was on the FP8-blockwise path, which has no engine query. #### Before enabling - **Size micro-batches well above m\*** (~4.5k tokens per micro-batch for Qwen3-8B, TP2, fast host): use dynamic batching with a large token budget. Do not benchmark FP8 RL at small micro-batches, and compare timings only on one host. - **Expect more memory**, from TE's FP8 copies. - **Keep importance-sampling correction on.** Matching lowers the systematic offset (KL, log-perplexity) more than the per-token spread: the dual-clip rate is similar for the matched and unmatched MXFP8 arms, about a third of FP8-TW's. - **On SGLang < 0.5.18, set `fp8_gemm_runner_backend=flashinfer_cutlass`.** The default Triton MXFP8 GEMM decodes ~2× slower than BF16. - **On SGLang, do not set `fp8_gemm_runner_backend=deep_gemm` on Blackwell.** Known limitation, not fixed here; a TODO in `mxfp8_refit_loader.py` records the fix. - A dense layer DeepGEMM cannot serve (N % 64 ≠ 0 or K % 128 ≠ 0) falls back to FlashInfer. At every sync SGLang 0.5.20 rebuilds that layer's FlashInfer scale into new storage, while the CUDA graphs captured at startup keep reading the old one, so decode would use a stale scale for that layer. - The post-sync self-check runs the layer eagerly and does not see it. Found by reading SGLang's code, not reproduced on hardware. - The default Blackwell backends (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL / CUTLASS) rebuild their scale in place and are not affected. - **On Blackwell, prefer MXFP8 to FP8-blockwise,** which needs power-of-two scales there (#8062). - **Watch `actor/entropy`** when switching recipes. #### What this does not show - **Short runs.** One seed per configuration and 3–60 steps; no claim about final quality. - **The matching experiment.** It runs only at the initial checkpoint and does not split the gain between weights, activations and kernels. - **FP8 KV cache in setting B.** All three arms of B ran vLLM with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` to shorten generation at 8192-token responses; A, C, D and the controlled runs keep the KV cache in BF16. - It is not MXFP8: K and V are stored as FP8 E4M3 with one scale per tensor (1.0), and on B200 vLLM 0.24 also quantizes Q to FP8 by default. - The learner has no KV cache and computes attention in BF16, so every sampler in B carries a quantization source the learner lacks, whatever its weights. - Comparisons within B stand, but B's absolute KL is not comparable with the other settings, and its BF16 arm is not BF16 end to end: step-1 KL 0.00610 vs. 0.00066 in A, a gap that B's data and response lengths also feed. The cache's share was not measured; switching only `kv_cache_dtype` at fixed weights would measure it. - **The byte check.** It covers 3 of 36 layers at two syncs, dense only. - **The break-even model.** It rests on one model and one host type. The profile covers one rank and one micro-batch size, and does not name the Python functions that carry the host time. - **MoE.** One model family, vLLM only, 10 steps; the FP8-blockwise path has no self-check. - **Fault injection.** The hardware campaign has not been run; CPU fault-injection tests are in `tests/utils`. ### Reproducing The arms of a setting differ only in their precision flags; model, data, seed, batch sizes, parallelism and learning rate are identical. | Arm | Flags added to the BF16 command line | |---|---| | FP8-TW / BF16 | `++actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.fp8="e4m3"` `++…fp8_recipe="tensorwise"` | | MXFP8 / BF16 | `++…fp8="e4m3"` `++…fp8_recipe="mxfp8"` | | MXFP8 / MXFP8 | `++…fp8="e4m3"` `++…fp8_recipe="mxfp8"` `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization=mxfp8` |
Setting A, BF16 arm: command line as resolved at runtime ```bash python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo --config-path=config --config-name=ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml \ data.train_files=/workspace/data/gsm8k/train.parquet \ data.val_files=/workspace/data/gsm8k/test.parquet \ data.return_raw_chat=True \ data.train_batch_size=64 \ data.max_prompt_length=1024 \ data.max_response_length=2048 \ data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \ data.truncation=error \ algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \ algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \ actor_rollout_ref.model.path=/workspace/models/Qwen3-8B \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=32 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size=2 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size=1 \ trainer.experiment_name=v3_nooff_bf16 \ trainer.n_gpus_per_node=2 \ trainer.nnodes=1 \ trainer.save_freq=-1 \ trainer.test_freq=999 \ trainer.total_epochs=100 \ trainer.total_training_steps=60 ```
How the other settings differ from A: - **B** uses DAPO-Math-17k, an 8192-token response cap, dynamic batching at 12,288 tokens per GPU, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` in every arm, and 32 steps. - **C** is A with `rollout.name=sglang` on SGLang 0.5.12, 30 steps. - **D** is Qwen3-30B-A3B on 4×B200 (TP2 × EP2), with dynamic batching at 20,480 tokens per GPU, parameter offload, a CPU optimizer, full recompute, FlashInfer autotuning off, and 10 steps. The controlled runs use A's command line with experiment-only hooks that time, log and dump data without changing the computation. ### API and Usage Example No API change; the mode is enabled through existing config: ```yaml # Training: Blackwell (SM100+), Megatron-Core >= 0.13, TE >= 2.1, Megatron-Bridge model path (default) actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config: fp8: "e4m3" # or "hybrid" fp8_recipe: "mxfp8" # 32-element block scaling # Rollout: vLLM (ModelOpt MXFP8) or SGLang (FP8 method in MXFP8 mode) actor_rollout_ref.rollout: name: vllm # or sglang quantization: mxfp8 ``` Weights stay BF16 in training (`fp8_param` is not supported), so checkpoints are unchanged; the sampler starts from the BF16 checkpoint and receives freshly quantized weights after every optimizer step. Guard switches, all read at call time: | Variable | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK` | on | `0` disables the post-sync self-check | | `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL`, `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL` | 0.25 | self-check tolerances | | `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT` | `warn` | `raise` makes mismatches fatal; `0` disables the audit | | `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL` | on | `0` disables the step sentinel | | `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX`, `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS` | 1.0, 2 | sentinel thresholds | ### Design & Code Changes **Training** - `verl/models/mcore/util.py`: - `_compute_fp8_thd_align_size` aligns each sequence to `lcm(32, align)` under MXFP8 (via mcore's `get_fp8_align_size`); blockwise is unchanged; - `get_fp8_padding_options` replaces five copies of the padding decision. - `model_forward.py`, `model_forward_fused.py`, `router_replay_utils.py`: pass `fp8_recipe` to every THD preprocess call. - `verl/utils/megatron_utils.py`: the legacy non-bridge path used to reset a requested FP8 config to BF16 silently. It now raises with a pointer to `use_mbridge=True`. No working configuration reaches this path: trainers always build a bridge, and `use_mbridge=False` has been rejected at engine init since #4528. - `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: rejects QAT combined with a TE FP8 recipe, since the two contracts conflict. **Shared quantizer.** `verl/utils/mxfp8_quant.py`: - `mxfp8_quantize`: TE `MXFP8Quantizer`, row-wise, 32-row padding, compact UE8M0 `[*, K/32]` scales; - `MXFP8_KEEP_HIGH_PRECISION_LAYERS = ("lm_head", "model.embed_tokens")`. **vLLM rollout** - `vllm_async_server.py`: `quantization: mxfp8` injects a config that vLLM normalizes to `ModelOptMxFp8Config`, with the MoE routers in `ignored_layers`. - `vllm_quant_utils.py`: recognizes the config and emits `weight` + `weight_scale` (uint8 `[N, K/32]`) per ModelOpt naming. - `vllm_fp8_utils.py`: registers the ModelOpt MXFP8 dense and MoE methods with the existing record/stage/reprocess/fold cycle, which keeps CUDA-graph-captured storage valid. The reprocess step clears vLLM's MoE "post-processing done" flag. - `mxfp8_exclusion_patch.py` (also in #7918): exact module-path exclusion matching, enabled only on configs verl generates (F2). - `utils.py`, `vllm_rollout.py`: `quantized_param_names`, through which the audit asks the live engine which parameters it holds in FP8. **SGLang rollout** - `sglang_mxfp8_utils.py`: launch config builder, sync-time quantizer helper (%32 shape check, errors propagate), and feature detection. - `async_sglang_server.py`, `sglang_rollout.py`: - `quantization: mxfp8` branches; - a guard against combining rollout quantization with the delta checkpoint engine, which would bypass quantization; - a warning that sglang < 0.5.18 defaults to the slow Triton MXFP8 GEMM. - `mxfp8_refit_loader.py`: after `load_weights`, re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` on every MXFP8 layer whose resolved backend keeps derived scale copies (F3). `flashinfer_trtllm` is rejected because it shuffles weights in place. **Guards** - `verl/utils/mxfp8_refit_check.py`: the post-sync self-check, for the dense probe and the MoE expert probe. - `verl/utils/quant_layer_audit.py`, hooked in `engine_workers.py` on the engine's weight export, so every sync route passes through it. It compares the learner's FP8 layer set with the sampler's rule and, on vLLM, with the live engine. - `verl/utils/quant_sentinel.py`, called from `ray_trainer.py` and `v1/trainer_base.py`. - `verl/utils/fp8_utils.py`: excludes the shared-expert gate from the SGLang sync's name rule. **Where quantization happens during a sync** - **Megatron → SGLang:** `ServerAdapter.update_weights` quantizes on the trainer side, then streams `(weight, weight_scale_inv)`. - **Megatron → vLLM:** the worker extension receives BF16 weights and quantizes them inside the vLLM process, then the refit cycle re-derives kernel layouts. **Which layers stay in high precision** | Component | Training | vLLM rollout | SGLang rollout | |---|---|---|---| | decoder linears (attention, MLP, MoE experts) | MXFP8 GEMMs (fprop, dgrad, wgrad) | MXFP8, quantized at each sync with TE's quantizer | same | | `lm_head`, token embedding | BF16 (not TE FP8 linears) | BF16 via `ignored_layers` | BF16 via `ignored_layers` and the sync name rule | | MoE router | BF16/FP32, outside FP8 GEMMs | BF16: excluded explicitly, because vLLM's gate inherits the model's quant config | BF16: SGLang builds routers without a quant config | | attention, norms, sampling | BF16 / FP32 | BF16 (KV cache BF16 unless `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`) | same | **Docs and tests** - `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`: an "MXFP8 Training (Blackwell)" section covering both engines, the consistency rationale, guards, the SGLang GEMM-backend choice and known issues. - `docs/low_precision/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.md`. - Ten CPU test files, listed under **Test**. ### AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude), including the code, the B200 experiment design, the measurement methodology and analysis in the validation section, and the figures. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, commissioned and reviewed the B200 runs, and can defend the design end to end, including: - why MXFP8 needs 32-token alignment in training (TE's columnwise wgrad layout) but not at inference; - why sharing TE's quantizer removes the weight-grid part of the train–inference mismatch but not the activation part; - how the refit cycle keeps CUDA-graph-captured storage stable across per-step weight updates. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting). - [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`, `docs/low_precision/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.md`. - [x] Add unit test(s): ten CPU test files (see **Test**); Blackwell end-to-end runs in **B200 validation**. - [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 # FP8 RL in verl
 
-Last updated: 09/29/2026
+Last updated: 10/13/2026
 
 verl supports two FP8 modes for accelerating RL training:
 
@@ -215,6 +215,301 @@ Results and observations:
 
 ---
 
+## MXFP8 Training (Blackwell)
+
+MXFP8 is the OCP microscaling FP8 format: E4M3 elements with one shared E8M0 scale per
+32-element block, natively accelerated by Blackwell tensor cores. Compared to the
+`blockwise` recipe above (1x128 activation / 128x128 weight scaling, designed for Hopper),
+MXFP8 uses hardware-decoded block scales and needs no `NVTE_FP8_BLOCK_SCALING_FP32_SCALES`
+workaround.
+
+### Requirements
+
+- **Blackwell GPUs** (SM100+). On Hopper, use `fp8_recipe: "blockwise"` as described in
+  the FP8 End-to-End section instead — Hopper tensor cores cannot consume MXFP8 block scales.
+- **Megatron-Core >= 0.13** and **Transformer Engine >= 2.1**
+
+### Key Configuration
+
+```yaml
+# MXFP8 training via Transformer Engine
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config:
+  fp8: "e4m3"                # element format; "hybrid" (e4m3 fwd + e5m2 bwd) also supported
+  fp8_recipe: "mxfp8"        # 32-element block scaling
+
+# MXFP8 rollout inference (SGLang)
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout:
+  name: sglang
+  quantization: mxfp8
+```
+
+Notes:
+
+- Training uses the Megatron-Bridge model path (`actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_mbridge=True`),
+  which is now the only Megatron model-building path in verl.
+- Model weights stay in bf16 (`fp8_param` is not supported); only GEMM inputs are cast to
+  MXFP8 on the fly, so checkpointing is unchanged.
+- verl pads packed sequences to the 32-token block boundaries MXFP8 quantization requires;
+  this is automatic once `fp8_recipe: "mxfp8"` is set.
+
+#### SGLang MXFP8 GEMM backend
+
+Which kernel SGLang uses for MXFP8 dense GEMMs depends on the SGLang version:
+
+- **sglang <= 0.5.17** (e.g. 0.5.12) runs them on a generic Triton kernel unless a FlashInfer
+  backend is requested. In a 2xB200 measurement, MXFP8 decode on that path was about 2x slower
+  than bf16 decode; the FlashInfer CUTLASS backend was about 1.3x slower than bf16 in the same
+  setup. verl logs a warning at launch on these versions when no backend is set. Select CUTLASS with
+
+  ```bash
+  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.sglang.fp8_gemm_runner_backend=flashinfer_cutlass
+  ```
+
+  (`fp8_gemm_runner_backend` is the `ServerArgs` field name; the CLI spelling
+  `--fp8-gemm-backend` is not accepted through `engine_kwargs`.)
+- **sglang >= 0.5.18** (sgl-project/sglang#33208) removed the Triton path. With no backend set,
+  Blackwell uses FlashInfer CuTe-DSL when available, otherwise FlashInfer CUTLASS; Hopper uses
+  DeepGEMM. No flag is needed.
+
+Two constraints on this path:
+
+- Every one of these FlashInfer / DeepGEMM backends derives a kernel-specific copy of the
+  weight scales at load time (`weight_scale_inv_swizzled` / `weight_scale_inv_deepgemm`), and
+  SGLang's weight-update path does not rebuild it. verl therefore registers an MXFP8 refit loader
+  (`mxfp8_refit_loader.py`) that re-runs the post-load processing after every weight sync; it reads
+  the backend each layer actually resolved to, so it covers the version-dependent defaults above.
+  A sync reaches SGLang as one update request per bucket, so the loader only loads on those
+  requests and re-derives once, on a closing request verl sends after the last bucket.
+  Without it the engine keeps serving load-time scales against freshly synced weights and generates
+  garbage from step 0. `flashinfer_trtllm` shuffles the weight tensor itself in place at load and is
+  rejected by the loader.
+- Do not set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` for an SGLang rollout: verl
+  launches SGLang with `enable_memory_saver=True`, and `torch_memory_saver` refuses that
+  allocator mode, killing the server in `load_model`. The vLLM path tolerates the variable.
+
+Neither engine showed an MXFP8 rollout throughput gain over bf16 in these runs (SGLang 0.5.12 and
+vLLM 0.24.0); the measurements are in the PR description.
+
+#### Guard rails for a quantized rollout
+
+Two failures met during the B200 validation were silent — the run kept going with exit code 0
+while every sample was garbage (a quantized `lm_head` producing `nan` logits; an engine serving
+stale kernel scale layouts after a weight sync). verl now fails loudly in both cases:
+
+- **Quantized-rollout sentinel** (trainer side, both trainers). When `rollout.quantization` is set,
+  the step metrics are checked after each step: non-finite `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean`,
+  `rollout_corr/kl` above 1.0 (typical values are 0.001–0.03), or every response hitting the
+  length cap on two consecutive steps raise a `RuntimeError` naming the likely causes. Disable
+  with `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL=0`; tune with `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` / `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS`.
+- **MXFP8 refit self-check** (engine side, vLLM and SGLang). After every weight sync the smallest
+  MXFP8 linear layer's own quantized GEMM is run on a small random input and compared with a
+  dequantized bf16 reference of the canonical weight and scale; a stale or mis-laid-out scale
+  shows up as O(1) relative error and raises. On SGLang one local expert of the smallest MXFP8 MoE
+  layer is probed the same way (every probe row routed to it, compared with the gated-MLP reference on
+  the dequantized `w13` / `w2`; tolerance `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL`, default = the linear one);
+  the probe makes up only the router logits (0 for the probed expert, -1e4 for the others) and runs
+  them through the model's own TopK, so each MoE runner gets the routing input it consumes — the
+  FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner, SGLang's default for MXFP8, routes inside the kernel and rejects a
+  precomputed top-k — and the reference reads `w13` in the order the engine stores it (`[up; gate]`
+  on TRT-LLM). It is skipped, with a warning, where such logits cannot pin one expert at weight 1
+  (sigmoid, grouped, biased or custom routing, fused shared experts, a routed scaling factor), under
+  expert parallelism, and under TP without `reduce_results`; a probe that raises is logged with the
+  exception type and the file and line it came from. Measured on 1×B200 with SGLang 0.5.20 and its
+  default TRT-LLM runner, the expert probe ran on every sync with a relative error of 0.049–0.054,
+  and raised (1.756) when the expert layout was deliberately re-derived twice. Before 10/13/2026 it
+  was always skipped on TRT-LLM (`MoE refit check skipped`, with an empty reason). On vLLM the same expert probe runs on `ModelOptMxFp8FusedMoE` layers by calling the
+  weight holder's `forward_modular` / `forward_monolithic` directly (skipped under expert or data
+  parallelism and for non-SiLU gates). vLLM 0.24's ModelOpt MXFP8 MoE method processes its weights
+  only once per layer and returns early afterwards; verl's patched hook clears that flag on every
+  refit so the kernel layout is re-derived from the synced scales. On SGLang MoE layers the loader additionally checks,
+  before re-deriving the kernel layout on the closing request of a sync, that the sync wrote every staged expert scale (the staging
+  buffer is pre-filled with the UE8M0 NaN code `0xFF`): experts whose HF names miss the sync-side
+  rule would otherwise arrive as a scale-less bf16 cast in the fp8 buffer. Scales the MoE runner
+  rewrites without changing their shape or dtype (FlashInfer TRT-LLM, the default, and CUTLASS on
+  SGLang ≤ 0.5.15) or leaves canonical (CUTLASS on ≥ 0.5.20) are not staged, so this check does
+  not cover them. The kernel-vs-reference probe compares the kernel's output with a reference
+  dequantized from the canonical weight and scale, so it catches stale or mis-laid-out derived
+  scales but not a sync that delivered wrong scale values. Neither do the sync-vs-engine dtype
+  check and the audit below: they compare dtypes and which layers are quantized, by parameter
+  name, not values. Disable both with `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=0`; the probe tolerance (default
+  0.25) is `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL`.
+- **Quantized-layer audit** (trainer worker, Megatron engine). "Matched" train/rollout quantization
+  presumes both sides quantize the same layers, but training decides implicitly (TE linear modules
+  inside `fp8_autocast`) and rollout decides by name blacklist (`ignored_layers`). At the first weight
+  sync after a training step, verl reads which decoder layers actually ran fp8 GEMMs (TE's fp8 weight
+  workspaces) and compares them, per synced parameter name, with the rollout side. The audit wraps the
+  training engine's weight export (`get_per_tensor_param`), which every sync route shares - the
+  colocated worker, the checkpoint engine and the server-replica path - and produces its verdict when
+  the weight stream ends. What "the rollout
+  side" is depends on the engine and every message says which: on vLLM the engine is asked directly
+  (`collective_rpc` into the worker, which resolves each HF name onto its live module with the sync's
+  own `is_fp8_weight` check and reports whether it is held in fp8; that check only recognizes
+  `LinearBase` and fused-MoE modules, so a quantized `ParallelLMHead` reads as not fp8 there, and a
+  quantized `lm_head` is reported only by the comparison with the configured rule); on SGLang there is
+  no return channel, so the trainer compares against the weight-sync
+  rule and the loader's sync-vs-engine dtype check (next bullet) covers the sync-to-engine half. It logs
+  each disagreement (e.g. `first_last_layers_bf16` without the matching rollout regex, a router the
+  name patterns miss, `lm_head` left in the quantized set, Mixtral's `w1/w2/w3` experts that the
+  SGLang sync-time include list does not match). On SGLang the rule evaluated is the sync-time
+  include/exclude rule in `verl/utils/fp8_utils.py`; a name it misses is shipped unquantized even
+  when the engine built that layer as fp8. Fused expert tensors as `transformers >= 5` saves them
+  (`mlp.experts.gate_up_proj`, no `.weight` suffix) are judged too. The signal survives
+  `param_offload=True` (verl marks each module before it drops the TE workspace cache on offload);
+  when there is no signal at all — `disable_parameter_transpose_cache=True` makes TE skip the cache —
+  the audit warns once that it cannot run instead of staying silent. `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=raise`
+  turns the report into an error, `=0` disables it.
+- **Sync-vs-engine dtype check** (SGLang loader). Before a sync is written into the engine, every
+  incoming linear weight's dtype is compared with the dtype of the engine parameter that will receive it
+  (HF names are mapped onto SGLang's fused modules: `q_proj` → `qkv_proj`, `gate_proj` → `gate_up_proj`,
+  per-expert names → the fused `w13` / `w2` tensors). A bf16 tensor headed for an fp8 parameter, or fp8
+  data headed for a bf16 one, is refused by name instead of being cast silently by `load_weights` —
+  e.g. Mixtral's `experts.N.w1/w2/w3`, which the sync rule does not match while the engine built them as
+  fp8. Disabled with `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=0`.
+- **MoE experts on SGLang.** With the fp8-serialized checkpoint a verl sync delivers, SGLang's MXFP8
+  MoE method rewrites expert tensors in place at load on the MoE runners SGLang allows for MXFP8 on
+  Blackwell, CUTLASS on SGLang ≥ 0.5.20 excepted: FlashInfer TRT-LLM (the default) reorders and
+  shuffles both the expert weights and their scales, CUTLASS swizzles the expert scales (SGLang
+  ≤ 0.5.15 keeps their `[E, N, K/32]` shape, 0.5.16 to 0.5.19 rebind them to the swizzled
+  tensor's own shape; ≥ 0.5.20 hands the canonical scales to the kernel and rewrites nothing),
+  and DeepGEMM packs them. Where
+  a scale's shape or dtype changed, the refit loader stages it back to the canonical layout for
+  `load_weights`; where it did not, `load_weights`
+  writes the canonical data over the live buffer. Either way the kernel layout is re-derived once
+  per sync, on the closing request, into the storage the CUDA graph captured. Until 10/12/2026
+  staging and re-deriving ran on every bucket, so a MoE sync spanning more than one bucket did not
+  work: layers a later bucket had not written yet were re-derived from the `0xFF` staging fill
+  (rejected by the written-scale check, or folded into the live buffer with the check off), and on
+  runners that keep the shape every layer outside the bucket had its rewrite applied once more,
+  silently, since nothing was staged for the check to inspect. Measured on 1×B200 (SGLang 0.5.12
+  with its default FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE runner; a 2-layer, 8-expert Qwen3-MoE at TP1; 4 steps):
+  with 1 MB buckets (12 requests per sync) the code before the fix re-derived every MoE layer on
+  each of the 12 requests, and after every sync the `w2` scales of 14 of the 16 experts held the
+  scales the sync had sent rewritten once for each re-derivation that ran after they arrived.
+  Nothing was reported, and `rollout_corr/kl` was 0.018–0.046 against 0.0001–0.0005 with a single
+  bucket. With the fix the same sync re-derived once, on the closing request, every expert's
+  scales matched, and the KL was back at the single-bucket level. The same comparison on SGLang
+  0.5.20 (the version verl locks) gave the same picture: before the fix 0 or 1 of each layer's 8
+  experts was served correctly (weights and scales) and `rollout_corr/kl` was 0.019–0.046,
+  silently; with it every expert was correct and the KL 0.0001–0.0005.
+- **Do not use SGLang's CUTLASS MoE runner for MXFP8 on SGLang 0.5.20**
+  (`engine_kwargs.sglang.moe_runner_backend=cutlass`). Its kernel reads the expert scales in the
+  layout SGLang's own CUTLASS quantizer writes, while for an fp8-serialized checkpoint — what a
+  verl sync delivers — SGLang 0.5.20 hands it the canonical scales unchanged (same FP8 values, the
+  scale bytes in a different order). Measured on 1×B200: every expert's output was about 0.8 off
+  (relative) with the engine holding exactly the bytes the sync sent, and `rollout_corr/kl` was
+  0.004–0.013 against 0.0001–0.0006 on the default FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner. The MoE refit
+  self-check fails the first sync in that configuration.
+
+### MXFP8 Rollout and Train-Inference Consistency
+
+With `quantization: mxfp8`, the rollout engine (SGLang or vLLM) is launched in MXFP8 mode
+against the bf16 checkpoint (via a `quantization_config` override, no offline conversion
+needed), and weight sync quantizes the bf16 actor weights to MXFP8 on the fly.
+
+For vLLM, the config maps to `ModelOptMxFp8Config` (weight `fp8_e4m3fn` + `uint8` UE8M0
+`weight_scale`), refits reuse the same pristine-layout staging cycle as the blockwise FP8
+path, and vLLM's Marlin/emulation fallbacks allow serving MXFP8 weights on pre-Blackwell
+GPUs (SM80+) — the served weight grid is still produced by TE's quantizer, so
+train-inference weight consistency is preserved regardless of the serving kernel.
+
+**Where the sync quantizes.** On vLLM the trainer sends bf16 tensors and the vLLM worker quantizes
+them on receipt (`quant_weights` in `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`). This reuses verl's existing
+vLLM FP8 refit path and is not required by MXFP8; SGLang quantizes on the trainer before sending, as its
+FP8 path already did. Two consequences:
+
+- The vLLM sync moves bf16 bytes: about 16.4 GB per sync for Qwen3-8B, against 9.7 GB if MXFP8 weights
+  plus scales were sent (the embedding and `lm_head` stay bf16 either way), and 61 GB against 32 GB for
+  Qwen3-30B-A3B. In the colocated B200 runs this did not dominate: MXFP8 added about 1 s per step to the
+  sync on Qwen3-8B (3.2 → 4.2 s), of which TE's quantization was about 11 ms of GPU time; most went to
+  restoring loadable layouts (0.57 s) and re-deriving kernel layouts (0.49 s), which the receiver does
+  wherever the quantization runs. Disaggregated deployments (the NCCL, Mooncake and other
+  checkpoint-engine backends) pay the full bf16 traffic. TODO: send MXFP8 weights plus scales from the
+  trainer — quantize the post-update bf16 weights with TE's `MXFP8Quantizer` as the SGLang path does, ask
+  the engine which parameters it holds in fp8 instead of re-deriving a name rule, and load E4M3 +
+  `weight_scale` through the same staged buffers. TE's cached FP8 weights are not a shortcut: TE
+  refreshes them on the next forward pass and verl drops them on offload, so at sync time they can still
+  hold the weights from before the last optimizer step.
+- The worker decides from the live engine which tensors to quantize: `is_fp8_weight(name, model)`
+  resolves each name onto the module that will receive it and checks whether its weight is fp8, so no
+  separate name rule has to agree with the engine (the sender-side SGLang path needs its sync-vs-engine
+  dtype check for that). Known gap: `is_fp8_weight` only recognizes `LinearBase` and fused-MoE modules,
+  while vLLM's ModelOpt config (0.24 and 0.29) also quantizes `ParallelLMHead` unless it is excluded. A
+  quantized `lm_head` therefore reads as not fp8: the sync sends it as bf16, the loader casts it into the
+  E4M3 parameter without a scale, and its `weight_scale` is never written. When refit staging allocates
+  a fresh buffer for that scale, as it does at TP=2, the buffer keeps its `0xFF` fill (the UE8M0 NaN
+  code) and every logit is NaN. Reading the code, this is how the `lm_head` NaN logits in the B200
+  validation arose; it has not been re-run on hardware. `lm_head` and the token embedding stay excluded
+  (`MXFP8_KEEP_HIGH_PRECISION_LAYERS`); TODO: judge the receiving parameter's dtype instead of the module
+  class.
+
+The staging cycle decides per layer whether a refit must go through stage → load → reprocess
+by comparing the live parameters with the checkpoint layout recorded at load. A kernel that
+hands back a *rewritten copy with the checkpoint's shape and dtype* is invisible to that
+comparison. FlashInfer TRT-LLM's MXFP8 MoE prep (`ModelOptMxFp8FusedMoE` on Blackwell: W13→W31
+swap, gate/up row interleave, tile shuffle of weights and scales) is such a kernel, so verl's
+patched `replace_parameter` records the rewrite when it sees it and the layer is staged on every
+refit. Measured on 1×B200 (vLLM 0.24, Qwen3-MoE tiny, TP1): the MoE expert probe read
+rel err 1.739 at the first sync before this record existed and 0.052 with it, same weights
+and inputs; the dense probe was 0.026 both times.
+
+**Known issue, bf16 MoE rollout on Blackwell (independent of MXFP8; tracked in verl-project/verl#7978).** With
+`quantization` unset, vLLM 0.24 auto-selects the FlashInfer TRT-LLM bf16 MoE backend on SM100,
+whose BlockMajorK layout turns `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` into 4-D tensors. verl's bf16 weight
+sync feeds `model.load_weights` per-expert 2-D tensors, which the loader can no longer index
+(`shard_dim=0 is not a valid data dimension for a 3D tensor`). The fix (wengeezhang/verl#4,
+upstream verl-project/verl#7987; awaiting hardware validation) stages the checkpoint layout as
+a view over the live storage -- the block layout keeps the byte count, or pads it -- so the
+buckets load straight into it, then re-derives the kernel layout layer by layer and copies it
+back into the storage the CUDA graph captured; the extra memory is one layer's temporary.
+Backends that keep the checkpoint shape (Triton, FlashInfer CUTLASS) are left alone. Without
+the fix, pin the layout-preserving backend:
+`+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.moe_backend=triton`. The same-shape staging fix
+described above was merged upstream as verl-project/verl#7986.
+
+The weight-sync quantization deliberately uses **TransformerEngine's `MXFP8Quantizer`** —
+the same quantizer the trainer's FP8 GEMMs apply to weights — so the rollout engine serves
+exactly the weight grid the training forward pass saw. An independent quantization kernel
+can round E8M0 scales differently at block boundaries and reintroduce train-inference
+mismatch. Residual mismatch (activation quantization kernels and GEMM implementations still
+differ between TE and SGLang) is small; pairing with token-level TIS is recommended,
+as with the blockwise FP8 E2E recipe.
+
+Layer skipping follows the same rules as FP8 rollout (`ignored_layers`,
+`modules_to_not_convert`, or the `SGLANG_FP8_IGNORED_LAYERS` env var). Layers whose
+last weight dim is not a multiple of 32 cannot be MXFP8-quantized and must be excluded
+this way — e.g. vision towers of VLMs (`SGLANG_FP8_IGNORED_LAYERS=visual`); weight sync
+fails with an actionable error if such a layer is selected. If you enable
+`first_last_layers_bf16` on the training side, keep the two sides consistent by excluding
+the same layers from rollout quantization, e.g. for a 36-layer model with the first and
+last layer in bf16:
+
+```json
+{
+  "quantization_config": {
+    "ignored_layers": ["re:model\\.layers\\.(0|35)\\..*"]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+**Learning dynamics (cause unresolved).** In the B200 runs (Qwen3-8B on gsm8k with vLLM and with
+SGLang, Qwen3-8B on DAPO-Math-17k with vLLM, Qwen3-30B-A3B on DAPO-Math-17k with vLLM; one seed each,
+10 to 60 steps), the policy's entropy under MXFP8 training with an MXFP8 rollout stayed flat or rose
+slightly (−4% to +6% from the first steps to the end of the run), while it decayed under bf16 (−7% to
+−49%) and FP8 tensorwise (−19% to −74%); the one FP8 blockwise run (Qwen3-30B-A3B, 10 steps) also rose
+(+9%). An MXFP8 learner with a bf16 rollout landed in between (−23% on gsm8k with vLLM), so the
+difference is carried by the trained weights, not only by the rollout's quantization. Training reward
+and held-out accuracy ended close to bf16. Compared at matched training reward, the MXFP8 runs on gsm8k
+and DAPO-Math-17k reached each reward level at the same step as bf16, with higher entropy. Compared at
+matched change from the initial policy (`actor/kl_loss` against the bf16 reference, minus each run's
+value at steps 1–3, which is mostly the precision offset), they moved as far as bf16 on gsm8k with vLLM,
+about a third less with SGLang, and about 5× less on DAPO-Math-17k. So the logs rule out slower reward
+learning over these horizons, but they do not tell whether the retained entropy is useful exploration or
+a smaller policy change; separating the two needs saved checkpoints evaluated on fixed contexts with a
+bf16 forward, which these runs did not keep. Until then, do not treat step-matched checkpoints from
+different recipes as the same point of training, and watch `actor/entropy` when switching recipes.
+

+# Opt-in MXFP8 exclusion patch
+
+Last updated: 10/13/2026
+
+## Status and scope
+
+The parser/matcher patches are registered in `build_fp8_method_patchers()` and
+installed through the existing `apply_vllm_quant_patches()` lifecycle. verl marks
+the mxfp8 `quantization_config` it generates for online rollout with
+`_verl_exact_mxfp8_exclusions: true` in `vLLMHttpServer._apply_quantization`, so the
+strict matcher is active for that config. Unmarked configs (checkpoints, other
+quantization methods) keep vLLM's original matching unchanged.
+
+vLLM's `ModelOptQuantConfigBase.is_layer_excluded()` (0.24 to 0.29) includes a legacy
+substring fallback. A router exclusion such as `model.layers.0.mlp.gate` also
+matches the dense SwiGLU `model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj`. Both HF projections
+(`gate_proj` and `up_proj`) can consequently remain unquantized in rollout.
+The upstream comment about ModelOpt 0.39 is not a runtime version guard.
+
+`build_mxfp8_exclusion_patchers()` supplies two wrappers on the
+`ModelOptMxFp8Config` subclass: `from_config()` transfers the explicit opt-in to
+the parsed instance; `is_layer_excluded()` uses strict matching only when that
+instance is marked. Unmarked configs call the original matcher. The ModelOpt
+base class, other quantization classes, and `get_quant_method()` are untouched.
+
+## Integration contract for the MXFP8 feature branch
+
+1. verl adds `_verl_exact_mxfp8_exclusions: true` only to the online MXFP8 HF
+   quantization config it generates itself (`_apply_quantization`, mxfp8 branch). Do
+   not add this marker to loaded user or checkpoint configs. Keep all real router/high-precision exclusions; this helper
+   fixes matching, not router discovery across model architectures.
+2. Install the common patches BEFORE vLLM parses that raw HF config. The parser
+   wrapper explicitly saves the boolean marker; upstream normalization need not
+   preserve unknown dictionary fields. Patching only after parsing loses provenance.
+3. In **each model-building worker**, install the common patches before creating
+   linear/MoE layers. Parsed configs carry only a boolean marker across serialization,
+   not instance-bound methods. Existing worker startup installs the common patches;
+   feature-branch integration must verify this also holds on its MXFP8 paths.
+   A driver-only patch or a post-refit call is insufficient.
+
+```python
+from verl.utils.vllm.mxfp8_exclusion_patch import VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS
+from verl.utils.vllm.vllm_quant_utils import apply_vllm_quant_patches
+
+# Future integration: ONLY the config generated by verl for online MXFP8.
+hf_quant_config = {
+    "quant_method": "mxfp8",
+    "ignored_layers": ["model.layers.0.mlp.gate", "lm_head", "model.embed_tokens"],
+    VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS: True,
+}
+
+# In the launcher, BEFORE creating/parsing the vLLM config:
+apply_vllm_quant_patches()
+# Pass hf_quant_config through hf_overrides["quantization_config"].
+# Each model-building worker must also call apply_vllm_quant_patches().
+```
+
+The example lists one layer for brevity; production integration must supply its
+complete policy and the actual raw config corresponding to the parsed instance.
+The marker is an explicit opt-in, not authentication or automatic proof of origin.
+The caller owns provenance. The common registry owns installation/idempotence
+via its existing `fp8_state.vllm_patches` guard. Builders return unstarted patchers,
+not independently installed global state. Invalid marked configs raise instead
+of silently leaving the legacy matcher active. The former instance-bound helper
+is replaced by these registered wrappers; no per-instance installation is needed.
+
+## Matching contract
+
+- An ordinary entry matches a module when it equals a run of whole dot-separated
+  components of the module's name: `lm_head` matches `lm_head` and
+  `language_model.lm_head`, `model.layers.0.mlp` matches its descendants such as
+  `model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj`, but `model.layers.0.mlp.gate` does not match
+  `model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj` and `lm_head` does not match `lm_head_extra`.
+  This keeps what the legacy substring fallback got right and drops only matches
+  that cut through a component. Wrapped names matter in practice: vLLM remaps
+  exclusions with the model's `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, whose rule `"lm_head."` →
+  `"language_model.lm_head."` (46 multimodal models in 0.29) does not apply to a
+  bare `lm_head`, so a VLM's `language_model.lm_head` is reached only by component
+  matching; an exact-only matcher would quantize it.
+- Case-sensitive `fnmatch`-style globs are supported, not `re:` expressions.
+- Patterns are evaluated against the fused runtime name and its HF shard names.
+  Literal matches are passed to vLLM's `is_layer_skipped()` so all-or-none shard
+  validation is preserved (including mixed exact/glob exclusions).
+- An explicit exclusion of the fused module applies to the whole module.
+- The upstream helper's specialized fused-expert-group handling is retained;
+  this is not a new per-expert precision policy.
+- Current `exclude_modules` and `packed_modules_mapping` are read on each call;
+  the helper does not cache exclusion decisions or change the weight-sync cache.
+
+## Validation
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py -q
+```
+
+CPU tests use lightweight vLLM doubles and check the 28-layer/56-HF-parameter
+collision, router preservation, instance isolation, legacy checkpoint behavior,
+explicit opt-in, invalid inputs, fused shards, globs, parser propagation, config
+serialization, registry integration, restoration, and old-vLLM fallback. They do not
+establish GPU kernel correctness or that the feature branch installed the helper
+in the correct worker.
+
+Before deployment, validate against the installed vLLM matcher and then rebuild
+the engine: check `gate_up_proj.quant_method`, weight dtype and scales on B200,
+check initial and post-training refits, and ensure engine recheck no longer finds
+the 56 gate/up discrepancies. Include a real MoE router regression and retain the
+refit self-check. Updating only an already-built model's config cannot rebuild
+its BF16 layers as MXFP8 layers.

+"""FP8 padding alignment for THD preprocessing, incl. the mxfp8 recipe."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+import verl.utils.device as device_module
+
+
+def _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size: int = 1, cp_size: int = 1, cp_rank: int = 0):
+    megatron = types.ModuleType("megatron")
+    core = types.ModuleType("megatron.core")
+    parallel_state = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.parallel_state")
+    packed_seq_params = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.packed_seq_params")
+
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_world_size = lambda: cp_size
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_rank = lambda: cp_rank
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_group = lambda: object()
+    parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size = lambda: tp_size
+
+    class PackedSeqParams:
+        def __init__(self, **kwargs):
+            self.__dict__.update(kwargs)
+
+    packed_seq_params.PackedSeqParams = PackedSeqParams
+
+    # Mirrors megatron.core.fp8_utils.get_fp8_align_size for CI hosts without megatron.
+    fp8_utils = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.fp8_utils")
+    fp8_utils.get_fp8_align_size = lambda fp8_recipe: 32 if fp8_recipe == "mxfp8" else 16
+
+    core.parallel_state = parallel_state
+    core.fp8_utils = fp8_utils
+    megatron.core = core
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron", megatron)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core", core)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core.parallel_state", parallel_state)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core.packed_seq_params", packed_seq_params)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core.fp8_utils", fp8_utils)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(device_module, "is_npu_available", False)
+
+    util_path = Path(__file__).parents[2] / "verl" / "models" / "mcore" / "util.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("mcore_util_fp8_padding", util_path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+def test_compute_fp8_thd_align_size(monkeypatch):
+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch)
+
+    # Default (blockwise & friends): per-seq lcm(16, align), total align*128.
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(1) == (16, 128)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(2) == (16, 256)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(2, "blockwise") == (16, 256)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(12) == (48, 12 * 128)
+
+    # mxfp8 scales in 32-element blocks: per-seq lcm(32, align).
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(1, "mxfp8") == (32, 128)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(2, "mxfp8") == (32, 256)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(12, "mxfp8") == (96, 12 * 128)
+
+
+def test_get_fp8_padding_options(monkeypatch):
+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch)
+
+    class FakeConfig:
+        fp8 = None
+        fp8_recipe = "mxfp8"
+
+    # fp8 disabled: no padding, recipe not forwarded.
+    assert mcore_util.get_fp8_padding_options(FakeConfig()) == (False, None)
+
+    config = FakeConfig()
+    config.fp8 = "e4m3"
+    assert mcore_util.get_fp8_padding_options(config) == (True, "mxfp8")
+
+    config.fp8 = "hybrid"
+    config.fp8_recipe = "blockwise"
+    assert mcore_util.get_fp8_padding_options(config) == (True, "blockwise")
+
+
+def _padded_seqlens(packed_seq_params) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return packed_seq_params.cu_seqlens_q_padded.diff()
+
+
+def test_preprocess_packed_seqs_mxfp8_alignment(monkeypatch):
+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size=1)
+
+    batch_size, seq_len = 2, 100
+    input_ids = torch.arange(batch_size * seq_len, dtype=torch.long).reshape(batch_size, seq_len)
+    attention_mask = torch.zeros(batch_size, seq_len, dtype=torch.bool)
+    attention_mask[0, :17] = True
+    attention_mask[1, :50] = True
+
+    _, params_default = mcore_util.preprocess_packed_seqs(
+        input_ids, attention_mask, pre_process=True, use_fp8_padding=True
+    )
+    seqlens_default = _padded_seqlens(params_default)
+    # Every sequence 16-aligned, total 128-aligned.
+    assert (seqlens_default % 16 == 0).all()
+    assert params_default.cu_seqlens_q_padded[-1] % 128 == 0
+
+    _, params_mxfp8 = mcore_util.preprocess_packed_seqs(
+        input_ids, attention_mask, pre_process=True, use_fp8_padding=True, fp8_recipe="mxfp8"
+    )
+    seqlens_mxfp8 = _padded_seqlens(params_mxfp8)
+    # Every sequence 32-aligned, total still 128-aligned.
+    assert (seqlens_mxfp8 % 32 == 0).all()
+    assert params_mxfp8.cu_seqlens_q_padded[-1] % 128 == 0
+
+
+def test_preprocess_thd_engine_mxfp8_alignment(monkeypatch):
+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size=1)
+
+    rows = [
+        torch.arange(17, dtype=torch.long),
+        torch.arange(50, dtype=torch.long),
+    ]
+    input_ids = torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(rows, layout=torch.jagged)
+
+    _, params_mxfp8, _ = mcore_util.preprocess_thd_engine(
+        input_ids, pre_process=True, use_fp8_padding=True, fp8_recipe="mxfp8"
+    )
+    seqlens_mxfp8 = _padded_seqlens(params_mxfp8)
+    assert (seqlens_mxfp8 % 32 == 0).all()
+    assert params_mxfp8.cu_seqlens_q_padded[-1] % 128 == 0

+"""CPU coverage of provenance, instance isolation and fused exclusion matching.
+
+The lightweight vLLM doubles model the relevant v0.24 matching behavior; no GPU,
+quantized weights, or optional vLLM installation is needed for this suite.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import pickle
+import sys
+from contextlib import ExitStack
+from fnmatch import fnmatchcase
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import ModuleType
+
+import pytest
+
+
+def _load_patch():
+    path = Path(__file__).parents[2] / "verl/utils/vllm/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("mxfp8_exclusion_patch_under_test", path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+def _is_layer_skipped(prefix, ignored_layers, fused_mapping):
+    """Model vLLM's exact-match helper, including fusion and expert-group handling."""
+    leaf = prefix.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
+    if leaf in fused_mapping:
+        if prefix in ignored_layers:
+            return True
+        parent, separator, _ = prefix.rpartition(".")
+        skipped = [parent + separator + shard in ignored_layers for shard in fused_mapping[leaf]]
+        if any(skipped) != all(skipped):
+            raise ValueError("All shards of fused layers must have the same precision")
+        return all(skipped)
+    if "experts" in prefix:
+        return any(prefix in entry for entry in ignored_layers if "experts" in entry)
+    return prefix in ignored_layers
+
+
+class _ModelOptBase:
+    packed_modules_mapping = {
+        "qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"],
+        "gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"],
+    }
+
+    def __init__(self, excluded):
+        self.exclude_modules = list(excluded)
+
+    def is_layer_excluded(self, prefix):
+        if _is_layer_skipped(prefix, self.exclude_modules, self.packed_modules_mapping):
+            return True
+        # The legacy ModelOpt fallback that causes the router/gate_up collision.
+        return any(p in prefix or fnmatchcase(prefix, p) for p in self.exclude_modules)
+
+    def get_quant_method(self, prefix):
+        return "UnquantizedLinearMethod" if self.is_layer_excluded(prefix) else "ModelOptMxFp8LinearMethod"
+
+
+class _MxFp8Config(_ModelOptBase):
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(cls, config):
+        # Mimic upstream normalization: unknown HF keys are not kept on the config.
+        return cls(config.get("ignored_layers", config.get("exclude_modules", [])))
+
+
+class _NvFp4Config(_ModelOptBase):
+    pass
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def patch_module(monkeypatch):
+    modelopt = ModuleType("vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.modelopt")
+    modelopt.ModelOptMxFp8Config = _MxFp8Config
+    quant_utils = ModuleType("vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils")
+    quant_utils.is_layer_skipped = _is_layer_skipped
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, modelopt.__name__, modelopt)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, quant_utils.__name__, quant_utils)
+    module = _load_patch()
+    with ExitStack() as stack:
+        for patcher in module.build_mxfp8_exclusion_patchers():
+            stack.enter_context(patcher)
+        yield module
+
+
+def _opt_in(patch_module, cfg):
+    return patch_module._mark_generated_config(
+        cfg,
+        hf_quant_config={"quant_method": "mxfp8", patch_module.VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS: True},
+    )
+
+
+def test_28_dense_layers_keep_gate_up_quantized_and_routers_excluded(patch_module):
+    cfg = _MxFp8Config([f"model.layers.{i}.mlp.gate" for i in range(28)] + ["lm_head", "model.embed_tokens"])
+    names = [f"model.layers.{i}.mlp.gate_up_proj" for i in range(28)]
+    # Each merged projection represents two HF parameters: reproduce 56 before patching.
+    assert sum(2 for name in names if cfg.is_layer_excluded(name)) == 56
+    assert _opt_in(patch_module, cfg)
+    assert sum(2 for name in names if cfg.is_layer_excluded(name)) == 0
+    for i in range(28):

+rather than an assertion at runtime. Reproduced on 2xB200 (Qwen3-8B / gsm8k):

+"""Engine-neutral MXFP8 quantization core shared by the SGLang and vLLM rollout paths."""
+
+import math
+import sys
+import types
+
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.mxfp8_quant import MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE, mxfp8_quantize
+
+
+def _install_fake_te(monkeypatch, recorded):
+    class FakeQuantized:
+        def __init__(self, data):
+            rows, k = data.shape
+            recorded["quantized_shape"] = (rows, k)
+            self._rowwise_data = data.to(torch.uint8)
+            scale_rows = math.ceil(rows / 128) * 128
+            scale_cols = math.ceil((k // MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE) / 4) * 4
+            self._rowwise_scale_inv = (
+                torch.arange(scale_rows * scale_cols, dtype=torch.float32)
+                .reshape(scale_rows, scale_cols)
+                .to(torch.uint8)
+            )
+
+    class FakeMXFP8Quantizer:
+        def __init__(self, fp8_dtype, rowwise, columnwise):
+            recorded["rowwise"] = rowwise
+            recorded["columnwise"] = columnwise
+
+        def quantize(self, tensor):
+            return FakeQuantized(tensor)
+
+    te = types.ModuleType("transformer_engine")
+    te_pytorch = types.ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch")
+    te_constants = types.ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.constants")
+    te_pytorch.MXFP8Quantizer = FakeMXFP8Quantizer
+    te_constants.TE_DType = {torch.float8_e4m3fn: "kFloat8E4M3"}
+    te.pytorch = te_pytorch
+    te_pytorch.constants = te_constants
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "transformer_engine", te)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "transformer_engine.pytorch", te_pytorch)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "transformer_engine.pytorch.constants", te_constants)
+
+
+def test_sglang_module_reexports_shared_core():
+    from verl.utils.sglang import sglang_mxfp8_utils
+
+    assert sglang_mxfp8_utils.mxfp8_quantize is mxfp8_quantize
+    assert sglang_mxfp8_utils.MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE == MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE
+
+
+def test_mxfp8_quantize_3d_expert_weight(monkeypatch):
+    # vLLM fused-MoE expert weights are 3D [num_experts, n, k]; the shared core
+    # must flatten leading dims, quantize, and restore the scale shape.
+    recorded = {}
+    _install_fake_te(monkeypatch, recorded)
+
+    weight = torch.randn(4, 16, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    qweight, scale = mxfp8_quantize(weight)
+
+    assert recorded["quantized_shape"] == (64, 64)
+    assert qweight.shape == (4, 16, 64)
+    assert qweight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    assert scale.shape == (4, 16, 64 // MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE)
+    assert scale.dtype == torch.uint8

+"""CPU tests for the MXFP8 post-refit self-check (dequant reference + probe)."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check import (
+    assert_mxfp8_linear_matches,
+    assert_mxfp8_moe_expert_matches,
+    mxfp8_dequantize,
+    mxfp8_moe_expert_reference,
+    probe_mxfp8_linear,
+    probe_mxfp8_moe_expert,
+)
+
+N, K = 16, 128
+
+
+def _fake_layer(seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    # fp8-representable values: small integers scaled by a per-block power of two
+    q = torch.randint(-6, 7, (N, K), generator=g).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.randint(120, 130, (N, K // 32), generator=g).to(torch.uint8)  # 2^-7 .. 2^2
+    return q, scale
+
+
+def test_dequantize_applies_per_block_power_of_two():
+    q = torch.ones(2, 64, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.tensor([[127, 128], [126, 130]], dtype=torch.uint8)  # 2^0, 2^1 / 2^-1, 2^3
+    w = mxfp8_dequantize(q, scale)
+    assert torch.equal(w[0, :32], torch.ones(32)) and torch.equal(w[0, 32:], torch.full((32,), 2.0))
+    assert torch.equal(w[1, :32], torch.full((32,), 0.5)) and torch.equal(w[1, 32:], torch.full((32,), 8.0))
+
+
+def test_dequantize_rejects_wrong_scale_shape():
+    q = torch.ones(2, 64, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        mxfp8_dequantize(q, torch.zeros(2, 3, dtype=torch.uint8))
+
+
+def test_probe_passes_for_a_correct_kernel():
+    q, scale = _fake_layer()
+    w = mxfp8_dequantize(q, scale)
+
+    def good_apply(x):  # what a healthy kernel computes, up to activation quantization noise
+        return (x.float() @ w.t()).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    rel = probe_mxfp8_linear(good_apply, q, scale)
+    assert rel < 0.02  # bf16 rounding only; real kernels add ~4% from activation quantization
+    assert assert_mxfp8_linear_matches("l0", good_apply, q, scale, engine="test") == pytest.approx(rel)
+
+

+class _TELinear(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A TE linear as it looks after the first fp8 forward: it holds a weight workspace."""
+
+    def __init__(self, quantized: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4, 64), requires_grad=False)
+        if quantized:
+            self._fp8_workspaces = {"weight": object()}
+
+
+class TransformerLayer(torch.nn.Module):  # name matters: the audit looks for *TransformerLayer*
+    def __init__(self, layer_number: int, quantized: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layer_number = layer_number  # mcore: 1-based, global across PP
+        self.self_attention = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.self_attention.linear_qkv = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.self_attention.linear_proj = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.mlp = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.mlp.linear_fc1 = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.mlp.linear_fc2 = _TELinear(quantized)
+
+
+class _Chunk(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, quantized_layers, n=N_LAYERS):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.embedding = torch.nn.Embedding(10, 4)
+        self.decoder = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.decoder.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([TransformerLayer(i + 1, i in quantized_layers) for i in range(n)])
+        self.output_layer = torch.nn.Linear(4, 10)  # mcore ColumnParallelLinear: never TE

+def _hf_names(n=N_LAYERS, router=None, experts=None):
+    """Qwen/Llama-style dense names; ``router`` adds a router weight per layer, ``experts`` a
+    (prefix, [leaf names]) pair adding two experts per layer, e.g. ("block_sparse_moe.experts", ["w1", "w2", "w3"])."""
+    names = ["model.embed_tokens.weight", "model.norm.weight", "lm_head.weight"]
+    for i in range(n):
+        p = f"model.layers.{i}."
+        names += [
+            p + "self_attn.q_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.k_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.v_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.o_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.q_norm.weight",
+            p + "mlp.gate_proj.weight",
+            p + "mlp.up_proj.weight",
+            p + "mlp.down_proj.weight",
+            p + "input_layernorm.weight",
+            p + "post_attention_layernorm.weight",
+        ]
+        if router:
+            names.append(p + router)
+        if experts:
+            prefix, leaves = experts
+            for e in range(2):
+                names += [f"{p}{prefix}.{e}.{leaf}.weight" for leaf in leaves]
+    return names
+

+    weights = [(n, torch.zeros(1)) for n in _hf_names()]
+    list(auditor.record(iter(weights)))
+    assert auditor.run([_Chunk(quantized_layers=set())]) is None and not auditor.done
+    assert "produced no verdict" not in caplog.text
+    list(auditor.record(iter(weights)))
+    assert auditor.run([_Chunk(quantized_layers=set())]) is None and auditor.done
+    assert "produced no verdict" in caplog.text and "_fp8_workspaces" in caplog.text
+    assert "0 of 4 decoder layers" in caplog.text
+

+def test_auditor_names_disable_parameter_transpose_cache_as_the_cause(caplog):
+    # mcore's TE wrappers expose config.disable_parameter_transpose_cache on the module; True means TE
+    # never caches the fp8 weight, so the audit reports the cause at the very first sync it sees it.
+    chunk = _Chunk(quantized_layers=set())
+    for m in chunk.modules():
+        if isinstance(m, _TELinear):
+            m.disable_parameter_transpose_cache = True
+    auditor = QuantLayerAuditor(_sglang_pred(), "warn")
+    list(auditor.record((n, torch.zeros(1)) for n in _hf_names()))
+    assert auditor.run([chunk]) is None and auditor.done
+    assert "disable_parameter_transpose_cache=True" in caplog.text and "produced no verdict" in caplog.text
